newsitem.title: USA: Eskimo Pie seen as good buy - NYT.
newsitem.headline: Eskimo Pie seen as good buy - NYT.

text.p: Eskimo Pie Corp's stock is trading at a low, but some analysts see the ice cream-treat maker as a buy, the New York Times said.
Last week, Eskimo Pie's chairman and chief executive David Clark resigned amid earnings disappointments. The stock has fallen from about $22 in May to close Friday at $16 a share, the newspaper said.
Eskimo Pie's stock is trading at less than 13 times earnings, compared to the Standard and Poor's 500, which trades at about 20 times earnings, the newspaper said.
Despite some of its problems, Eskimo Pie still holds one of the strongest corporate brand names and one of the most widely-recognized names in frozen novelty treats, the newspaper said.
Analysts also cited Eskimo Pie's low capital expense structure and existing licensing agreements with Nabisco and Weight Watchers as reasons for optimism, the newspaper said.
Cyclical products like ice cream stocks also are often cheaper in the off-season, the newspaper said.
Since the stock is trading at low levels, analysts told the New York Times that "there can't be much of a disappointment."
